evidence.note: The file tests/genome/spawn-message-export-risk-warning.test.js does NOT exist in main. However, the retry-rate feature itself was implemented in the genome repo (PR #484) and documented in the leadflow repo via PR #1913. This branch contains additional integration tests specifically for the export-risk-warning portion of that work — it is unclear whether these tests are complementary to the genome-side implementation or superseded by it.

reasons: Branch contains only a new test file — no production code changes.
No deletions or modifications to existing files.
Test targets genome-level spawn-message export risk warning logic.
The genome repo (not this repo) is the canonical location for that logic; tests in this repo for genome internals are unconventional.
The retry-rate feature was resolved via an alternative approach (merge-only rescue in genome PR #484) — these tests may cover a discarded implementation path.

recommendation: Human review needed to decide whether tests/genome/spawn-message-export-risk-warning.test.js should be merged, adapted, or dropped. Key questions: (1) Does the genome PR #484 / spawn-message-builder.js already cover the export-risk-warning behavior these tests target? (2) Should integration tests for genome internals live in the leadflow repo at all, or should they be in the genome repo (LeonidaTheGreat/openclaw-genome)? If the tests are still valid and the behavior untested elsewhere, merge via a new task+PR. If the genome tests already cover this, safe to delete the branch.
